parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, TaskService. It is a single application service for a small task-tracking domain. It manages users, projects and tasks, and these are closely related because a task needs a project and an optional assignee. All persistence goes through the injected domain repository interfaces. All failures use the domain error types. Validation helpers (requireProject, requireUser, requireText, parseDueDate, isTaskStatus) are private and reused across methods, so each rule has one implementation. Two small repetitions exist: the "status must be todo, in progress, or done" message appears in both createTask and listTasks, and the status literals are hardcoded in isTaskStatus. These are minor and don't split the module into unrelated concerns or bypass its abstractions. I can't see the domain files, so I can't tell whether the domain already exports a status list that isTaskStatus should use. That uncertainty is why confidence is not higher.
